title: Research
text:
My research combines time-resolved spectroscopy, optical-frequency-comb instrumentation, and materials photophysics. The central aim is to measure ultrafast processes accurately and relate them to the chemical and structural evolution of the sample.


01



AI-NS combines asynchronously generated laser pulses with interferometric detection. It provides a broad temporal dynamic range, high spectral resolution, and rapid data acquisition without conventional mechanical delay scanning. My work includes AI-TA implementations across near-ultraviolet, near-infrared, and mid-infrared spectral regions.


Methods: AI-NS · AI-TA · ASOPS · coherent averaging · optical frequency combs




02



Ultrafast measurements are performed while the sample undergoes slower photochemical or structural change. This approach links carrier and exciton dynamics to processes such as photoinduced halide exchange and nanoplatelet aggregation.


Focus: real-time measurement · photoinduced reactions · heterogeneous samples




03



Transient absorption, photoluminescence, and complementary spectroscopy are used to determine how charges and excitons are generated, transferred, and relaxed in molecular and solid-state systems.


Systems: perovskites · organic chromophores · OLED emitters · photovoltaic materials




04



Mid-infrared AI-TA directly probes band-edge carrier relaxation and coupled structural dynamics in narrow-bandgap semiconductors, including tellurium and InAs.


Topics: band-edge carriers · coherent phonons · structural relaxation

title: Gi Rim Han

zerokelvin@korea.ac.kr




Understanding light-driven matter across time scales


Experimental physical chemist specializing in ultrafast spectroscopy

I am a research professor at the IBS Center for Molecular Spectroscopy and Dynamics, Korea University. My research focuses on developing and applying asynchronous and interferometric nonlinear spectroscopy (AI-NS) and optical-frequency-comb techniques to investigate ultrafast dynamics in molecules and functional materials.
My work connects custom instrumentation with photophysical analysis, including charge-carrier, exciton, and phonon dynamics in perovskites, organic optoelectronic materials, and narrow-bandgap semiconductors. I also use in situ measurements to follow ultrafast responses while materials undergo slower photochemical or structural changes.
